issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method has a different parameter list than the specification and the solution. The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect findStockIngredient(String): StockIngredient (single parameter), but the template defines findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive). This mismatch will confuse students and cause compile/runtime issues when following the UML or using the example calls (e.g., Main and other code expect a single-argument method).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and solution by providing a single-argument method: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Either change the existing method signature to the single-parameter variant or add an overloaded convenience method (findStockIngredient(String name)) that delegates to the two-parameter implementation. Ensure example calls (e.g., Main) compile and that behavior (case sensitivity) is documented/consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement and the reference solution define Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single-parameter). The template implementation, however, declares findStockIngredient(String, boolean caseSensitive) with a different signature. This mismatch forces students to reconcile two different method signatures for the same conceptual operation (finding an ingredient in stock), can cause compilation confusion in the template, and creates extraneous cognitive load when mapping the problem requirements to the provided starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's Stock.findStockIngredient method to match the problem statement and solution signature: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Remove the extra boolean parameter (or provide an overload) and implement the intended comparison logic inside the single-parameter method so the starter code and documentation reference the same identifier and signature.
